subject: ACME streaming benchmark scope — reproducibility & measurement next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@acme-retail.com>, Eva Li <eva@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Mar 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: ACME streaming benchmark scope — reproducibility & measurement next steps

Thanks for the call today — quick recap and concrete next steps so we can get the streaming qualification scheduled. High level items we agreed on: 

- SLO targets: 95th pct latency (tail) for streaming responses: 250ms per token for 20-token bursts, median latency target 90ms. Throughput target: sustained 250 QPS equivalent when measured as concurrent streaming sessions (see notes).
- Concurrency model: ACME will validate against a mix of 1:5 short chat (avg 20 tokens) and 1:1 long stream (avg 200 tokens) to simulate search+assist flows. Peak concurrency target: 120 simultaneous sessions.
- Measurement definitions: we will run the Redwood harness against a canonical prompt set you provide (see attachment), capture end-to-end ingress-to-first-token and per-token latency, and record CPU/GPU utilization and KV cache hit metrics. Reproducibility requires: seed prompt file + harness config + versioned model artifact.

Deliverables & owners: 
- ACME: export a representative prompt sample CSV (10k rows recommended) + labelled buckets (short/long). Due: Mon 2028-03-05 — Eva (owned).
- Redwood: provide harness config template and runbook + initial run on Redwood Dedicated (non-prod) to validate measurement pipeline. Due: Wed 2028-03-07 — Ben (owned).
- Joint: agree on acceptance criteria matrix and QA gating for fallbacks (model variant, region). Draft SLO matrix attached (slo_matrix_acme.xlsx). Due: Fri 2028-03-09 — Marissa (owned).

Notes on reproducibility: please ensure prompt CSV includes exact tokenization boundary notes (UTF-8, no trimming) and a small canonical seed set (100 prompts) that we pin for regression runs. Our harness will version the config file and embed timestamps; we also recommend saving the first-run logs and the model hash so later runs can be compared byte-for-byte.

Attachments: acme_prompt_samples_v1.csv (placeholder sample), redwood_harness_config.yaml (template), slo_matrix_acme.xlsx (draft acceptance matrix).

Next meeting: schedule a 30-minute sync after ACME shares prompt sample to finalize run window and staging credentials. I’ll send a meeting invite once Eva confirms availability.

Thanks —
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
T: +1 415-555-0199

From: Tom Reynolds <tom@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Eva Li <eva@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Mar 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME streaming benchmark scope — reproducibility & measurement next steps

Thanks Marissa — that aligns with what we discussed. Quick clarifications from ACME side: 

1) For the throughput target, when you say 250 QPS equivalent, do you mean 250 streaming sessions started per second, or 250 parallel active streams measuring per-token throughput? We intend to measure by active streams (concurrent sessions).
2) For the prompt CSV, we have some PII redaction rules. Is it okay to include placeholders for user data (e.g., [REDACTED_NAME])? We want the semantics preserved but no real PII.
3) Can Redwood run the initial pilot in eu-west-1 as well to validate region routing? We prefer testing in our primary prod region later, but pilot in us-west is fine.

We’ll start assembling the 10k row sample and the 100 canonical seed prompts. Eva, can you take point on the sample and share by Monday?

—Tom
Director, Platform Engineering
ACME Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@acme-retail.com>, Eva Li <eva@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

On Fri, 01 Mar 2028 at 16:42 Tom Reynolds <tom@acme-retail.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — that aligns with what we discussed. Quick clarifications from ACME side: 
> 
> 1) For the throughput target, when you say 250 QPS equivalent, do you mean 250 streaming sessions started per second, or 250 parallel active streams measuring per-token throughput? We intend to measure by active streams (concurrent sessions).

Thanks for flagging — we meant concurrent active streams; I’ll update the scope doc. For clarity in the harness: 250 concurrent sessions with the mixed short/long distribution above. 

> 2) For the prompt CSV, we have some PII redaction rules. Is it okay to include placeholders for user data (e.g., [REDACTED_NAME])? We want the semantics preserved but no real PII.

Yes — placeholders are fine as long as tokenization characteristics remain representative (same lengths and punctuation). Please include an extra column called "redaction_note" with a short explanation per row when possible. 

> 3) Can Redwood run the initial pilot in eu-west-1 as well to validate region routing? We prefer testing in our primary prod region later, but pilot in us-west is fine.

We can run the pilot in eu-west-1. For the joint run we’ll do two short validation runs: one in us-west-2 (Redwood staging) and one in eu-west-1. Ben — can you take the eu-west validation and confirm costs/availability?

Action: Eva to upload prompt CSV to the shared Drive link by EOD Mon. Ben to provision eu-west staging run and post the harness config we’ll use (redwood_harness_config.yaml) by Wed. I’ll draft the final acceptance matrix and post comments in the Drive doc.

Thanks —
Marissa
